newsitem.title: FRANCE: Havas Adv chief sees more TV sponsoring.
newsitem.headline: Havas Adv chief sees more TV sponsoring.

text.p: Alain de Pouzilhac, chairman of Havas unit Havas Advertising, said his company would suggest more and more to its clients that they sponsor the making of TV programmes.
In an interview with advertising industry weekly Strategies published on Friday, de Pouzilhac said Havas Advertising had to adjust to the way the advertising world is changing.

"Look at what is happening in media, with CanalSatellite or TPS. We are moving towards increasingly fragmented audiences," he said, referring to French digital satellite TV services Television Par Satellite (TPS), operated by TF1, and Canalsatellite, owned by Canal Plus.
"Programme making and the method of distribution will play an increasingly important role. The audience could double depending on the match, the film or the programme that you schedule," he said.
"The more we manage to associate the advertiser upstream, at the level of programme making, the more his audience can be guaranteed," he said.
De Pouzilhac said Havas Advertising would not seek to invest in programme making.

"That is not our function. The group will propose to its clients that they be associated with programmes very upstream. Our aim is to place our clients in the best possible audience context," he said.
Havas's recent accord with Compagnie Generale des Eaux and Canal Plus created a dynamic and synergies in line with the changes in advertising media, he said.
"All modern communication groups should cover programme making, programme distribution and obviously, the means to finance programmes," he said.

"The potential synergies between broadcasting, represented by Canal Plus, and the multimedia activities of the Havas group, via CEP, Havas Media Communication or Havas Advertising, are very strong," he said.
Asked if advertising would still exist in its current form, de Pouzilhac said he expected one-to-one marketing to take a good third of advertising on a world scale in the next five years.

"One-to-one, that is, the direct relation between advertiser and consumer, covers databases and interactive multimedia. In reality, this type of marketing marks the beginning of the end of mass media," he said.
